about: Effects of the privileges, laws, reforms, societal values and parliament agendas the campaign has held, from the game's definition files and English localization (tools/government_catalog.py). Generated: edit the tool, not this file.

al_caid.name: Al-Qā'id
al_caid.desc: By appointing a loyal Qā'id to oversee provinces and regulate trade on behalf of the state, we empower urban merchants while ensuring provincial governance. Our central treasury draws a stable customs revenue from the Qā'ids' supervised markets, and our tax-farms become a predictable cornerstone of state finance rather than the unstable patchwork they replaced. This institutional layer of provincial trade-administration gives the Maghrebi treasuries a steady commercial revenue that surrounding states cannot replicate.

andalusi_elite.name: Andalusi Elites
andalusi_elite.desc: The advance in has led to a talent drain of skilled Andalusi notables from Iberia. We are but one of the states who is willing to welcome those refugees with open arms and open positions in the government.

building_rights.name: Building Rights
building_rights.desc: Developing our settlements and cities is a costly endeavor. By granting building rights to the local population, we will ultimately reduce the overall end cost of development. However, giving the people such an allowance will considerably increase their influence.

clergy_land_rights.name: Religious Land Rights
clergy_land_rights.desc: We have decided to give the faithful the right to own private land. This will make them more powerful and influential, but will also allow for a more constant presence of holy men at our disposal.

modifiers.label: Possible clergy in Towns and Cities
modifiers.text: Possible clergy in Towns and Cities +0.1

clergy_literacy_rights.name: Religious Literacy Rights
clergy_literacy_rights.desc: Our religion has many associated works of literature containing the practices, morals, and principles of our faith. Our Clergy should have unlimited access to the written word in order to study the holy texts of our faith.

clerical_advisory_council.name: Religious Advisory Council
clerical_advisory_council.desc: We have decided to form a council of advisors, comprised entirely of holy Clergy. This will make them more influential, but also more complacent, as they will be able to express their concerns directly to us and see their interests satisfied.

communal_lands.name: Communal Lands
communal_lands.desc: Despite the inherently disadvantaged position of the common people, we must nevertheless dictate that all members of the Commoners have the right to establish common flocks of animals and to raise crops in shared fields.

dhimmi_administrative_posts.name: Grant Administrative Posts
dhimmi_administrative_posts.desc: Our borders are home to many who do not follow our state religion. Their local leaders are keen on maintaining their positions and beliefs. To cooperate with them and share in their wisdom is the natural path to a healthy administration.

dhimmi_military_service.name: Allow Military Service
dhimmi_military_service.desc: The many heathen believers who peacefully occupy our lands are more than willing to defend their livelihoods and their families, should we permit their recruitment.

dhimmi_pact_of_umar.name: Pact of Umar
dhimmi_pact_of_umar.desc: This treaty clearly defines the status, rights, and responsibilities of 'protected persons' within our realm, including Christians, Jews, Zoroastrians, and many other recognized faiths.

dhimmi_promote_tolerance.name: Promote Tolerance
dhimmi_promote_tolerance.desc: Our people frequently cite a desire to build a more diverse and tolerant society. Acting on their behest and following their example, we will treat non-believers with kindness as we strive to achieve stability and prosperity.

feudal_mercenary_contracts.name: Feudal Mercenary Contracts
feudal_mercenary_contracts.desc: The armies levied by our people often leave a lot to be desired. In order to protect our people and best our rivals, we must rely on foreign mercenaries, whose contracts will be managed by the elite members of our society.

gra_ulema_council.name: Council of the 'Ulamā'
gra_ulema_council.desc: The scholars of Islamic law serve as the supreme advisory council of our realm, interpreting religious doctrine and lending religious legitimacy to the sultan's governance. Their authority over legal matters ensures that the administration of justice remains rooted in the divine law.

gra_visirate.name: Vizierate
gra_visirate.desc: The vizierate is an office of high counsel through which noble administrators govern in the sultan's name, bringing order to the affairs of state and ensuring that capable hands guide the realm.

gra_volunteers_of_faith.name: Volunteers of the Faith
gra_volunteers_of_faith.desc: The mutaṭawwi'a are pious volunteers who join the sultan's forces in times of war against the infidel, driven by religious conviction rather than feudal obligation. Their numbers swell the ranks of our armies, and their fervor in battle more than compensates for their lack of formal military training.

jewish_court_financier_charter.name: Court Financier Charter
jewish_court_financier_charter.desc: Jewish merchants and bankers are appointed as official financiers to the royal court, handling currency exchange, long-distance credit, and luxury procurement. Their international networks expand our merchant presence, but displace established trading houses and alarm the clergy.

jewish_physician_exemption.name: Physician Exemption
jewish_physician_exemption.desc: Jewish physicians are granted royal license to practice medicine at court and throughout the realm, exempt from guild restrictions and canonical prohibitions. Their learning advances the state of medicine, though the clergy objects to heretics attending Christian patients.

market_fairs.name: Market Fairs
market_fairs.desc: The financing and development of merchant centers will surely attract higher trade traffic, while simultaneously amassing great wealth, ample quantities of various exotic goods, and a reputation for security.

noble_marriage_rights.name: Royal Marriage Rights
noble_marriage_rights.desc: The Nobility of our country are considered to be peers to our rulers. Therefore, they are eligible to marry into the ruling family, subsequently increasing their influence and power at court, as well as in the government.

noble_sponsored_navy.name: Noble Navy
noble_sponsored_navy.desc: Our navy is maintained and controlled by the Nobility. Thanks to their financial contributions, we will be able to raise a mighty fleet, although in exchange for permitting the Nobility to have more influences over naval affairs.

nobles_land_rights.name: Land Rights
nobles_land_rights.desc: This represents the privileges our Nobility have over the lands they rule and the people who inhabit them. Among those rights, Nobility can usually tax the Commoners living on their lands, draft them to form levies, or mete out justice on their own. These holdings are usually hereditary.

peasants_allowed_weapons_privilege.name: Common Militias
peasants_allowed_weapons_privilege.desc: The common people are allowed to keep their weapons, which they then must use when called for levy service.

peasants_free_peasantry.name: Free Mobility for the Common People
peasants_free_peasantry.desc: People are the most valuable asset of any state. Famines and discord would be the norm without them. Yet, the elites see them only as property — as possessions to hoard upon their ill-gotten lands!\nBy granting free mobility to the masses, their fate will be own hands once again, allowing them to leave the lands of their former masters and move to new, more fruitful fields.

primacy_of_nobility.name: Primacy of Nobility
primacy_of_nobility.desc: The Nobility of our country has proven to be key allies, as they support most of our enterprises and are the backbone of our armies. For this reason, they consider themselves our equals, and they have become so crucial to the government that we must consult with them before making important decisions.

sponsor_maritime_contracts.name: Sponsored Maritime Contracts
sponsor_maritime_contracts.desc: Maritime trade is a valuable source of revenue for our treasury. By granting exclusive contracts to our Burghers, we can regulate commerce while ensuring consistent tax income from shipping and trade.

treasury_rights.name: Treasury Rights
treasury_rights.desc: By granting the oversight of our treasury to wealthy, powerful members of our society, we will secure their interests and increase their loyalty to us, albeit at the expense of losing some tax revenue.

catalan_merchant_privileges.name: Catalan Merchant Privileges
catalan_merchant_privileges.desc: The Catalan merchants of are active in this country's ports and have received extensive privileges. Part of the duties collected from trading with them is passed onto the mother country, and this state receives the benefit of foreign mercenaries in return.

the_jewel_of_alandalus_reform.name: The Jewel of Al-'Andalus
the_jewel_of_alandalus_reform.desc: We are the only surviving member of the formerly Muslim realms that populated Al-'Andalus in the past. Huge Muslim empires have risen and fallen throughout Iberia, fragmenting in the process. As one of those fragmented parts, it is our destiny to reunify the people of Iberia under our banner.

modifiers.label: War Score vs other Religion Efficiency
modifiers.text: War Score vs other Religion Efficiency +10%

autonomous_councils.name: Autonomous Councils
autonomous_councils.desc: Our state consists of many different smaller states, each with their own customs and laws. All provinces, governed by their own councils, contribute to the central authority and align their policies along common lines.

central_councils.name: Central Council
central_councils.desc: The state is administrated as a single council wherein the members decide the policy of the state. Remote areas of our country will struggle to make their voice heard.

local_courts_administration.name: Local Courts
local_courts_administration.desc: The state rescinds many of their central powers in favor of local courts, which adapt their own administrations to best suit the needs and ways of the local population.

feudal_administration.name: Feudal Administration
feudal_administration.desc: We do not rule directly, but through subjects who swear loyalty to us. Influential members of the Nobility whose fealty can be assured are commanded to advise rulers of our subject nations of our pronouncements, which helps breed and maintain loyalty to the Crown.

confederal_union.name: Confederal Union
confederal_union.desc: A union of other, autonomous states which are the supreme authorities of their territories. The central government is limited to handling foreign politics, while internal affairs are resolved by the states.

federal_state.name: Federal State
federal_state.desc: The state is an amalgamation of many different smaller states with their own customs and laws. All states, however, are under the rule of the federal government and as such are subject to federal laws.

unitary_administration.name: Unitary Administration
unitary_administration.desc: The state is administrated as a single entity where the central government is the supreme authority of the nation. The provinces have little to say over the internal politics of the country.

pyatina_policy.name: Pyatina Division
pyatina_policy.desc: The Pyatina is the highest administrative division in Novgorod's government. The republic is divided into five Pyatinas, four of which border the city of Novgorod directly, while the fifth encompasses more distant territories.

eyalet_division.name: Eyalet Division
eyalet_division.desc: The Eyalet administration is the primary division of the . Every eyalet is ruled by a pasha, who in turn answers to the central government's Grand Vizier. The central laws of the state do not have to apply to every eyalet, and each pasha is free to incorporate local customs and mores to better rule their people.

merindad_policy.name: Merindad Division
merindad_policy.desc: A Merindad is a geographical-administrative division in the kingdoms of , , and . Merindads serve as intermediate administrative bodies between the central authority, the towns, and noble holdings. The head of a Merindad is the Merino, entrusted with administrative and judicial powers over their assigned territory as a representative of the ruler.

calpixque_system_policy.name: Calpixque System
calpixque_system_policy.desc: This Nahua governance system has evolved beyond its initial structure of hereditary tlatoani leaders. Provinces are now administered by appointed officials: local stewards called calpixque, and high stewards called huecalpixque. These officials manage the provincial tribute system under the supervision of the petlacalcatl in the capital. In particularly unruly provinces, military governors known as cuauhtlatoani may be appointed to maintain control.

tongues_policy.name: Tongues Division
tongues_policy.desc: The Tongue, or Langue System, categorizes members and assets based on ethnolinguistic divisions. Each Tongue is further subdivided into Priories, Grand Priories, Bailiwicks, and Commanderies. Each Langue has a designated headquarters, known as an auberge, located in the capital of the Order.

rajya_policy.name: Rajya
rajya_policy.desc: The Rajyas are the main provinces of the . These territories are each jointly governed by a military commander and a member of the ruling dynasty. Administration is carried out in the region's native language, which allows these laws to be implemented more effectively.

poligar_system_policy.name: Palaiyakkarars
poligar_system_policy.desc: Our lands are home to numerous unincorporated tribes and clans who could provide valuable service to the state, if properly integrated into our administrative system. As a class, these Palaiyakkarar officials would serve as law enforcement, fortification builders, provincial representatives, and military officers. Most importantly, they could mobilize their kinsmen to provide us with a steady supply of capable manpower.

zabt_system_policy.name: Zabt System
zabt_system_policy.desc: It is in the best interest of our state to encourage economic productivity, while simultaneously keeping a constant watch over regional economies. However, we have not always been successful in our administrative efforts, as ruling over the economic activities of so many subjects requires significant amounts of both human and material resources.\nIn order to solve this, we have created the zabt System, which establishes regular cadastral surveys to measure agricultural land, assess crop productivity, and classify land quality. Based on these surveys, standardized revenue rates are calculated and collected in cash rather than in-kind. This creates predictable, systematic taxation that ensures our state revenue reflects our actual agricultural capacity.

pronoia_system.name: Prónoia System
pronoia_system.desc: The Prónoia System functions as a means of temporarily transferring imperial fiscal rights, such as taxes or income from various sources, to individuals or institutions. Unlike the feudal system prevalent in Europe at the time, Prónoia grants were neither hereditary nor transferable, and ultimate ownership remained with the Emperor. In exchange for these privileges, the system ultimately served the purpose for the head of state to raise an army in times of need, and entailed that the troops had to mostly cover their own expenses.

komnenian_formalization.name: Komnénian Prónoia
komnenian_formalization.desc: Under the Komnénian emperors, the informal Prónoia system had been codified into a rigorous instrument of imperial policy. Grants were formally contracted, with each holder obligated to furnish a cavalry contingent proportional to the revenues they received. The Emperor retained the right of revocation, and a reorganised imperial registry tracked every grant and its associated military obligation ensuring that the land revenues of the realm translated directly into mounted levy strength under the crown's direct control.

palaeologan_hereditary_transition.name: Palaiológian Hereditary Prónoia
palaeologan_hereditary_transition.desc: Facing an exhausted treasury and the constant pressure of civil war and foreign invasion, the Palaeologan emperors have conceded the irrevocable.\nPrónoia grants are henceforth hereditary. Noble families who previously served at imperial pleasure now hold their lands as permanent patrimony, bolstering the legitimacy of the dynasty through aristocratic loyalty but at the cost of the military obligations that once gave the system its purpose. The cavalry that the grants were meant to fund must increasingly be hired at the state's own expense.

reformed_pronoia_system.name: Reformed Prónoia System
reformed_pronoia_system.desc: Rather than allow the Prónoia governors to strengthen their hold on their lands, the system has been changed so any loopholes that made the title of governor hereditary or transferable can no longer be exploited.

adelantamiento_system.name: Adelantamiento System
adelantamiento_system.desc: Led by an Adelantado, the Adelantamiento is an administrative system developed in by which members of the Nobility are placed as governors over frontier or newly conquered territories, reporting directly to the ruler. Adelantados have broad military, judicial, and administrative authority in these remote regions, and often finance expeditions themselves in exchange for land and expanded governing rights.

decentralized_trade_federations.name: Decentralized Trade Federation
decentralized_trade_federations.desc: We have delegated control over local economic affairs and business practices to the Nobility governors in those regions. This should help us greatly expand our trade network.

regulations_of_the_royal_court.name: Regulations of the Royal Court
regulations_of_the_royal_court.desc: A series of documents denoting the main functions of our government, from coronation ceremony etiquette, to the daily activities of the Crown, to the maintenance of our army. This framework serves as a robust basis for our government and the privy council known as savaziro.

maj_office_of_the_mahapatih.name: Office of the Mahapatih
maj_office_of_the_mahapatih.desc: Equivalent in status to a prime minister, the Mahapatih has tremendous influence in our political sphere. As the second in command over the entire nation, whoever holds this office is charged with overseeing critical affairs of the state, such as military expansion and the effective operation of the government.

no_censorship.name: No Censorship
no_censorship.desc: Free-thinking ideals are both uncontroversial and encouraged. artists are more likely to settle and remain in a country where they can freely express themselves, although there are inevitably zealots who oppose such liberty.

limited_censorship.name: Limited Censorship
limited_censorship.desc: The Clergy has some tolerance for heretical and controversial thinking, but their patience must not be tried.\n\nartists may leave or refrain from settling in a country, depending on how their work and peers are treated.

strict_censorship.name: Strict Censorship
strict_censorship.desc: There is no tolerance for heretical thinking. The Clergy watches over everything, and will not hesitate to punish those who do not conform.\n\nartists are less likely to settle or remain in a country unless they are adherents of the current religious doctrine.

de_heretico_comburendo.name: De Heretico Comburendo
de_heretico_comburendo.desc: Heresy is not tolerated in any aspect of society, and is punishable by burning at the stake. Religious services, writings, and opinions of a heretical nature will be purged.\n\nartists are likely to avoid settling or remaining in our country, and religious minorities will see their property confiscated and be subject to persecution.

doktrinalnaya_ohrana.name: Oprichniki Raids Permitted
doktrinalnaya_ohrana.desc: The Church is not immune to the purges of the , and members of the Clergy, particularly those who were perceived as a threat, are targeted. Monasteries are regularly pillaged, and monks are subjected to violence. Strict censorship is extended to theological works, religious texts, and historical writings, and people who adhere to different forms of are viewed with suspicion.

mandate_of_ofen.name: Mandate of Ofen
mandate_of_ofen.desc: The Mandate of Ofen will guide our approach to handling the spread of heresy in our country. It will not only dictate what we condemn as heretical, but will also mandate that every parish church must read it aloud to their congregations twice each year to reinforce its statutes among our people.

gold_and_silver_coins.name: Gold and Silver Coins
gold_and_silver_coins.desc: The metals selected for the coinage of our currency are gold and silver, for two different sets of coins.

gold_coins.name: Gold Coins Only
gold_coins.desc: We only use gold as the metal selected for the coinage of our currency.

silver_coins.name: Silver Coins Only
silver_coins.desc: We only use silver as the metal selected for the coinage of our currency.

bullion_coins.name: Bullion Coins
bullion_coins.desc: The metals selected for the coinage of our currency are silver and copper, using different mixtures.

barter_exchange.name: Barter Exchange
barter_exchange.desc: Different goods and materials, such as livestock, cloth, shells, cacao, etc., may be used as a common currency for trade.

stavraton_coin_policy.name: Stavraton Coins
stavraton_coin_policy.desc: Derived from a mixture of pure silver and some copper, the Stavraton is meant to replace the defunct hyperpyron in an attempt to revive the economy and modernize exchange rates.

martial_society.name: Martial Society
martial_society.desc: Martial values have always been important in our society, but as we expand our borders, the need for militarization becomes ever more apparent. We must continue this trend, and build a strong nation with military might at its core.

civil_society.name: Civil Society
civil_society.desc: A strong nation requires more than military might — it needs a dynamic civil society where artisans, traders, clerics, and institutions of all kinds can flourish, creating prosperous communities that generate wealth, maintain social order, and contribute to the development of a sophisticated state.

maritime_society.name: Maritime Society
maritime_society.desc: Our maritime traditions form the very fabric of our society. United in the thrill of taming the sea and venturing into foreign ports, our people have built a name for themselves as masters of naval affairs.

pietism_society.name: Prussian Virtues
pietism_society.desc: The virtues of Pietism — diligence, sincerity, and a sense of duty above all — are the core values of our society.

plc_sarmatism.name: Sarmatism
plc_sarmatism.desc: Our society originated with the ancient Sarmatians. However, Sarmatism is not just a theory of origin, but a cultural and political phenomenon that promotes the ideals of and the .

dhimmi_status_policy.name: Protected Dhimmi Communities
dhimmi_status_policy.desc: Non-Muslim subjects are granted formal protection under Islamic law, paying the jizya in exchange for freedom of worship. Their commerce enriches the realm's markets while slowing the pace of religious conversion.

dhimmi_persecution_policy.name: Restrict the Dhimmi
dhimmi_persecution_policy.desc: Pressure is placed on non-Muslim communities to convert or depart, clearing the realm of heterodox subjects and strengthening the faith's hold over the land.

dop_traditional_distribution_of_power.name: Traditional Distribution
dop_traditional_distribution_of_power.desc: Power is traditionally distributed among the ruling sovereign and the leading elites of our society. It does not challenge the status, and is favorable to neither the head of the state nor to the aristocracy.

dop_favor_the_ruler.name: Favor the Ruler
dop_favor_the_ruler.desc: The balance of power should favor the head of state, as they alone can be trusted to have the best interests of the nation at heart.

dop_favor_the_nobles.name: Favor the Elites
dop_favor_the_nobles.desc: The Nobility form the backbone of our society, and we could not do without their leadership. We would do well to cultivate their influence.

dop_favor_the_burghers.name: Favor the Wealthy
dop_favor_the_burghers.desc: The guilds and Burghers are the lifeblood of our people! And, of course, our treasury. We would do well to cultivate their influence.

modifiers.label: Prefers Court Language to be Market Language
modifiers.text: Prefers Court Language to be Market Language +1.5

dop_favor_the_clergy.name: Favor the Clergy
dop_favor_the_clergy.desc: Our faith has held our society together in the face of adversity time and time again, thanks to the guidance of our wise Clergy. We would do well to cultivate their influence.

modifiers.label: Prefers Court Language to be Liturgical Language
modifiers.text: Prefers Court Language to be Liturgical Language +1.5

dop_favor_the_clergy_catholic.name: Favor the Church
dop_favor_the_clergy_catholic.desc: The is the cornerstone of our realm. By elevating our Clergy in matters of governance, we strengthen our ties with rome_holy_city and open the coffers of the faithful. We would do well to cultivate their influence.

modifiers.label: Prefers Court Language to be Liturgical Language
modifiers.text: Prefers Court Language to be Liturgical Language +1.5

dop_favor_the_commoners.name: Favor the Common People
dop_favor_the_commoners.desc: The Commoners are the ones who toil daily to provide the basic resources, such as food, that everyone needs regardless of their social status. They, perhaps more than anyone, wish to raise our domain to new heights of prosperity and greatness. We would do well to cultivate their influence.

modifiers.label: Prefers Court Language to be Common Language
modifiers.text: Prefers Court Language to be Common Language +1.5

dop_law_gbara.name: Gbara
dop_law_gbara.desc: The Gbara is the deliberative assembly of and is defined in the constitution, the . The Nobility represent the many clans in our state, and check the power of the ruling .

dop_law_english_parliament.name: Parliament
dop_law_english_parliament.desc: Parliament is the de facto successor of the Magnum Concilium, and a major pillar of the government. Parliament's primary function is to check the power of the by requiring mandatory consultation on taxation and legislation, preventing absolute rule.

dop_law_navarrese_courts.name: Cortes de Navarra
dop_law_navarrese_courts.desc: The Nobility, the Clergy, and the Burghers have formed a deliberative assembly called the Cortes de Navarra, which has the duty to approve laws and taxes, and to investigate legal transgressions. While all Estates debate together, each of them votes as a separate assembly. The position of each Estate is previously decided internally by the majority. In order to achieve a resolution to any issue they deliberate, all Three Estates must agree on the action. Their power allows them to dethrone and elect rulers when needed, and overall to keep the power of the monarch in check.

dop_law_governing_senate.name: Governing Senate
dop_law_governing_senate.desc: The Governing Senate is the highest governmental body of the Russian State, and has been created as a replacement of the Boyar Duma. Combining the roles of the legislative, judicial, and executive powers, the Senate is a powerful institution which is subordinate to none but the rulers themselves.

dop_law_state_council.name: State Council
dop_law_state_council.desc: The State Council is the supreme state advisory body of , created to act as a mediating party between the autocratic regime and the regional Dumas introduced by the reform. The State Council examines proposed laws and oversees the budget and state expenditures, although it lacks the authority to propose changes. Instead, it makes recommendations based on the current situation.

dop_law_estates_general.name: Estates General
dop_law_estates_general.desc: The Estates General is the assembly of the feudal government of . It has a legislative and consultative role, and represents the three estates of the country: the Nobility, the Clergy, and the Commoners, which itself encompasses the Burghers. Unlike other Parliaments and Assemblies, the approval of the Estates General when making adjustments to the law, such as tax increases, is optional.

dop_law_assemblee_nationale.name: Assemblée Nationale
dop_law_assemblee_nationale.desc: Born from the ashes of the Ancien Régime, the Assemblée Nationale is the conversion of the old Estates General into a modern parliament. The Nobility and Clergy are no longer the dominant powers of the assembly, while the Burghers and the Commoners take a more active role in the events of the State.

dop_law_castilian_courts.name: Cortes de Castilla
dop_law_castilian_courts.desc: The Cortes de Castilla represent the estates and several cities with voting rights in the .

dop_law_comuneros_parliament.name: Empowered Cortes
dop_law_comuneros_parliament.desc: The Cortes, our Parliament, has been empowered as the primary political force in our country thanks to the efforts and fight of the Comuneros.

dop_law_castilian_courts_reinforced.name: Reinforced Cortes de Castilla
dop_law_castilian_courts_reinforced.desc: As a result of the Revolt of the Comuneros, Crown will now have a stronger grip on the Cortes de Castilla.

dop_favor_the_kontors.name: Favor the Kontors
dop_favor_the_kontors.desc: The Hanseatic Kontor is the basis of our financial success. The many offices we hold across serve as diplomatic ties between us and the host countries, as well as providing seats of power for our local Burghers.

dop_office_of_the_eristavi.name: Office of the Eristavi
dop_office_of_the_eristavi.desc: One of the most influential cornerstones of our administration, the title of Eristavi is granted to powerful noble families, allowing them the undisputed authority to recruit and lead armies under their banner. Those who hold this office also enjoy a dominant position in our internal affairs.

modifiers.label: Head of the Cabinet Promotion Cost Modifier
modifiers.text: Head of the Cabinet Promotion Cost Modifier -33%

dop_rudolfine_house_rules.name: Reformed House Rules
dop_rudolfine_house_rules.desc: The Reformed House Rules are a system of joint governance for the Austrian lands, granting all male family members equal status while reserving special privileges for the eldest.

cat_constitucions_de_catalunya_policy.name: Constitucions de Catalunya
cat_constitucions_de_catalunya_policy.desc: The constitutional framework of Catalonia binds the crown to respect the laws and liberties of its subjects — no new law may be enacted without the consent of the Corts, and the parliament's voice carries the weight of centuries of precedent.

nav_fueros_policy.name: Navarrese Fueros
nav_fueros_policy.desc: The ancient charters of Navarre guarantee the rights and customs of its people against royal encroachment, with each new monarch swearing to uphold the fueros before the kingdom's laws apply to them.

uneducated_masses_education.name: Uneducated Masses
uneducated_masses_education.desc: What use are reading and writing to those whose sole purpose is to tend crops? The masses are best left to their fields and flocks, innocent of the many dangerous ideas hidden between book covers.

basic_religious_education.name: Religious Teachings
basic_religious_education.desc: The millennia-old, tried-and-true method of letting our religious institutions take responsibility for educating our people, while the state focuses on more important tasks.

theocratic_education.name: Devout Education
theocratic_education.desc: A pious education, focusing on ensuring that students are well-versed in the workings of the divine. Theology can be more useful than mathematics, after all... albeit perhaps not in every situation.

apprenticeships_education.name: Individual Apprenticeships
apprenticeships_education.desc: The sacred process by which a skilled mentor passes down a lifetime of knowledge to a protégé. While many of these mentorship-apprentice arrangements are formally arranged, eager learners can also be taught by their families, established elder members of society, or even their guild quartermasters.

oral_tradition_education.name: Oral Tradition
oral_tradition_education.desc: Wisdom is passed down to younger generations through methods such as storytelling or the performing arts. Venerable members of a community tell and re-tell ancient tales and the lessons learned from them, which young listeners will memorize and repeat in the future. In this way, the history of our people will be preserved from generation to generation by those who lived it.

scottish_presbyterian_education.name: Presbyterian Education
scottish_presbyterian_education.desc: Our Church will be responsible for educating the people of our nation. These efforts will be financially supported through tax revenue collected from upon the landowning elite.

personal_religious_education.name: Personal Religious Education
personal_religious_education.desc: Why centralize education in formal institutions when the printing-press has allowed every household to become its own school? We will let our people educate themselves, giving them the responsibility of deciding what knowledge they find worthy of acquiring.

epic_tradition_education_sects.name: Epic Tradition
epic_tradition_education_sects.desc: Young people learn best when the knowledge is presented in the form of gripping, memorable tales, and they are both captivating and easy to understand. Much can be learned from the fantastic stories of our ancestors, and we shall make sure our people understand these lessons well.

epic_tradition_education.name: Epic Tradition
epic_tradition_education.desc: Young people learn best when the knowledge is presented in the form of gripping, memorable tales, and they are both captivating and easy to understand. Much can be learned from the fantastic stories of our ancestors, and we shall make sure our people understand these lessons well.

secular_education.name: Secular Education
secular_education.desc: Houses of worship are the home of the divine, not the classroom. Let us keep secular and religious instruction separate, as the mundane and divine realms are.

vedic_education.name: Vedic Education
vedic_education.desc: An education method that teaches the masses about Hinduism without seperating anyone into castes.

by_tradition.name: By Tradition
by_tradition.desc: Customary laws are commonly known and practiced in our country. Famous compilations of medieval customs include De Legibus et Consuetudinibus Angliae for England, Sachsenspiegel for northern Germany, or the Usatges of Barcelona for Catalonia.

by_blood.name: By Blood
by_blood.desc: The laws of our country reflect the nature of our people and the sovereign authority of our ruler, as expressed in the famous formula rex in regno suo est imperator regni sui - 'The king is emperor in his own kingdom.'

heir_special_succession.name: Special Succession
heir_special_succession.desc: The religion of the heir is not determined by the laws but by the heir_selection itself.

heir_same_religion.name: Same Religion
heir_same_religion.desc: Selecting the heir from the same religion as the prevailing one ensures that the beliefs and practices of the population and Crown are aligned. While this policy can contribute to religious cohesion, it may also limit opportunities for those of different faiths to assume leadership positions.

heir_same_religion_group.name: Same Religious Group
heir_same_religion_group.desc: Selecting the heir from the same religious group is often desirable in order to maintain religious and cultural continuity and prevent potential religious conflicts. This policy can help safeguard the stability of the realm by minimizing religious divisions within the leadership, at the expense of individuals from faiths considered to be 'heathen' being able to assume leadership roles.

heir_any_religion.name: Any Religion
heir_any_religion.desc: Faith is personal, and does not reflect nor compromise an individual's ability to lead. The heir may worship any religion and still assume leadership roles. This policy carries a higher risk of religious conflicts within the leadership, while promoting religious freedom and general acceptance.

open_borders_law.name: Open Borders
open_borders_law.desc: The borders of our country are open to anyone, and all may come and go freely.

closed_borders_law.name: Closed Borders
closed_borders_law.desc: Nobody is permitted to leave or enter our country.

efficient_tax_farming.name: Tax Farming
efficient_tax_farming.desc: Effectively collecting property taxes is the backbone of our national economy. Despite what the Commoners might advocate for, this revenue is vital for funding various projects, endeavors, and campaigns. As such, the accumulation of revenue and the general administration thereof should be entrusted to methodical Iqṭā' holders.

jagir_taxation.name: Jāgir Taxation
jagir_taxation.desc: The Jāgir system grants land and the right to collect taxes to appointees of the state, known as Jagirdars. Over the decades since its inception, the system has evolved so that the ruling body retains administrative and military authority, while Jagirdars collect taxes and turn over a portion of that revenue to the treasury.

land_acquisition.name: Land Acquisition
land_acquisition.desc: Administrating the vast lands under our jurisdiction is no simple matter. Let us strive to bring the territories closer to our central authority by reasserting our possession of these lands, in spite of protests from the Commoners.

lenient_taxation.name: Lenient Taxation
lenient_taxation.desc: Our people, regardless of their origin and faith, have long suffered under the taxation of the local Muqṭi'. Let us give them a helping hand by reducing their tax burden.

traditional_law_policy.name: Traditional Law
traditional_law_policy.desc: There are a plethora of informal punitive systems developed by communities based on their customs, traditions, and values. These legal systems have been passed down orally from generation to generation and are deeply rooted in the culture and history of the community.\n\nThe strength of Traditional Law lies in its ability to reflect the unique needs and values of a particular community. It is based on a shared understanding of what is right and wrong, and is often seen as more legitimate and accessible than formal legal systems. However, it can also be limited by its insularity and lack of flexibility.

civil_law_policy.name: Civil Law
civil_law_policy.desc: Civil Law, a legal system with roots in ancient Rome, is known for its precise written codification of laws and regulations. However, the rigidity of its structure can hinder the adaptation required to address the evolving needs of the people. Nonetheless, Civil Law can bring peace and stability to even the most turbulent nation.

common_law_policy.name: Common Law
common_law_policy.desc: Common Law is a legal system that originated amongst the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms. It is characterized by a reliance on precedent; judges are bound by their previous decisions rather than strict adherence to the written law of the state. This allows for a degree of predictability and consistency in legal decisions, but can also make it difficult to adapt to changing circumstances and may lead to the entrenchment of unjust or outdated laws.

vlach_law_policy.name: Vlach Law
vlach_law_policy.desc: Uniquely blending pastoral traditions and legal norms, the Vlach Law encapsulates a distinct system governing communities across medieval Europe. It affirms the rights to travel, bear arms, and practice hunting while sparing them from mandatory labor for landowners, instead paying taxes in livestock or coin. Furthermore, it institutes a binding military service commitment tailored to each realm, creating a network of and legal heritage.

sharia_law_policy.name: sharia Law
sharia_law_policy.desc: sharia Law is a comprehensive and deeply entrenched legal system in Islamic countries that governs many aspects of life, from personal conduct to matters of state. It has provided stability and continuity for centuries, but its strict and sometimes harsh penalties can be controversial and divisive.

modifiers.label: Prefers Court Language to be Liturgical Language
modifiers.text: Prefers Court Language to be Liturgical Language +3

matrilineal_customary_law_policy.name: Matrilineal Customary Law
matrilineal_customary_law_policy.desc: Codify the traditional customs of the realm, recognizing inheritance through the female line while allowing rulers of either gender.

pyrenean_law_policy.name: Pyrenean Law
pyrenean_law_policy.desc: Pyrenean Law is a legal system native to the peoples living around the Pyrenean Mountains. Despite the fact that this law was influenced by both the Civil Law and the Gothic Law, it remained different from them. Based on traditional customs and practices, this legal system is so embedded in our culture than rulers are obliogated to adapt to it, rather than overriding it with their own systems.

russkaya_pravda_policy.name: Russkaya Pravda
russkaya_pravda_policy.desc: This was the legal code of Kievan Rus', heavily influenced by their Norse origins. It has been rewritten many times over the centuries since its inception, and is the main source of Old Russian Law.

pskov_judicial_charter_policy.name: Pskov Judicial Charter
pskov_judicial_charter_policy.desc: The Pskov Judicial Charter is the Old Russian legal code which was built on the Russkaya Pravda. It emcompasses many important features of the political, social, and economic life within Pskov.

novgorod_judicial_charter_policy.name: Novgorod Judicial Charter
novgorod_judicial_charter_policy.desc: The Novgorod Judicial Charter is an Old Russian legal code which codifies many common practices within Novgorod. It also sets and defines the four positions in the Novgorodian court and covers the administrative matters of the state.

bav_codex_bavarica.name: Upper Bavarian Land Rights
bav_codex_bavarica.desc: The 'Upper Bavarian Land Rights' is a collection of old Bavarian legal codes which codifies many common practices within Bavaria. It also sets and defines the role of the Nobility in Bavaria's court and covers administrative matters of the state.

cyfraith_hywel_policy.name: Cyfraith Hywel
cyfraith_hywel_policy.desc: Welsh Law, also known as Cyfraith Hywel, is a unique legal system that emerged from the ancient customs of Wales. It differs from both Common Law and Civil Law in that it emphasizes restorative justice, placing a greater emphasis on compensation and reconciliation rather than punishment. The law was created by the Welsh kings and princes to promote unity and order among the Welsh people, and is known for its complexity and adherence to precedent.

fetha_negest_policy.name: Fetha Negest
fetha_negest_policy.desc: The Fetha Negest, or Justice of the Kings, is a theocratic legal code compiled by Abu'l-Fada'il ibn al-Assal, and is a significant work of justice. Drawing from apostolic writings and Byzantine law codes, it encompasses ecclesiastical and secular matters, and is further influenced by Roman law.

ordinances_of_justice.name: Ordinances of Justice
ordinances_of_justice.desc: A set of legal frameworks aimed at curbing the power of influential that do not align themselves with the agenda of our central authority. These sets of jurisprudence aim at pushing back against a powerful noble class.

consiglio_maggiore.name: Consiglio Maggiore
consiglio_maggiore.desc: A body of aristocrats and various classes of citizens, including and artisans as well as bankers, the Consiglio Maggiore is in charge of the autocratic apparatus within our Republic.

maiestas_carolina.name: Maiestas Carolina
maiestas_carolina.desc: A set of laws and articles, drafted to greatly curb the power of the Nobility. The code entails the passing of noble property to the state in certain circumstances, as well as limiting the arbitrary powers of the Nobility throughout our realm.

byzantine_law.name: Byzantine Law
byzantine_law.desc: Byzantine law, evolving from Roman law with Christian and Hellenistic influence, largely derives from Justinian's Corpus Juris Civilis, which emphasizes ceremonial emperor roles, and reflects philosophical and religious ideals.

law_of_the_pious_emperor.name: Law of the Pious Emperor
law_of_the_pious_emperor.desc: A compendium of translated books of law and great works of ancient philosophy into the Serbian language, issued by Emperor .

goryeon_code_policy.name: Goryeon Code
goryeon_code_policy.desc: The Goryeon Code, also known as Gyeongje Yukjeon - Six Codes of Governance - is the code of law of Korea. Shaped by the Chinese bureaucratic arts, this code has prevailed in our state for centuries.

joseon_code_policy.name: Joseon Code
joseon_code_policy.desc: The Joseon Code, also known as Gyeongguk Daejeon - National Code - is the revision of the old Goryeon Code. With the founding of a new dynasty, many laws and traditions of the previous code have been compiled anew in the current code.

chi_ming_dynasty_code_policy.name: The Great Code
chi_ming_dynasty_code_policy.desc: The Great Code shall be created to address all the critical problems that our dynasty faces and the ones that our predecessors faced. It will ensure that we will not fall to corruption and ministerial abuses of power!

mll_leges_palatinae.name: Leges Palatinae
mll_leges_palatinae.desc: Leges Palatinae shall strengthen the power of our court along with legitimizing our right as a independent state.

scottish_civil_law.name: Scottish Civil Law
scottish_civil_law.desc: The College of Justice has reformed our Civil Law towards a new standard. This Institution consists of well-educated members of our country, who will rule on any important topic concerning the Scots Law.

sobornoye_ulozheniye_policy.name: Sobornoye Ulozheniye
sobornoye_ulozheniye_policy.desc: The Sobornoye Ulozheniye serves as a foundational legal and social code that adapts the laws to fit a country with a strong centralized state and a clear social hierarchy. It builds upon the prevalent code and incorporates certain elements from the Byzantine code of law, solidifying class distinctions, and codifying a legal system that reflects the prevailing political and religious influences of the time.

piotrokow_wislica_statutes.name: Piotrków-Wiślica Statutes
piotrokow_wislica_statutes.desc: A set of statutes that shape our legislation and offer a robust frame for the future of our people, these statutes are comprehensive and extremely influential. Their jurisdiction impacts various aspects of our society, from private to public law and the responsibilities of each social class.

dan_regional_law.name: Regional Laws of Denmark
dan_regional_law.desc: The legal Codes of Jutland, Zealand, and Scania grants us regional legal systems. While prone to regionalism, it will represent the will of the Danish people.

dan_danske_lov.name: Danske Lov
dan_danske_lov.desc: A unified legal code for our country will bring a new standardized legal framework for our government to work in and our subjects to appeal to.

laws_of_burgos.name: Laws of Burgos
laws_of_burgos.desc: This set of laws provides the legal framework for our activities and subjects in the colonial territories. It is especially concerned with the rights of the native population and their organization into the encomiendas system.

new_laws_indies.name: Leyes Nuevas
new_laws_indies.desc: The New Laws serve as an improved version building upon the Laws of Burgos, strengthening the control that we can assert in our colonial possessions.

siete_partidas_law.name: Siete Partidas
siete_partidas_law.desc: The Siete Partidas is a compilation of statutory laws made by Alfonso X of Castile with the intention of uniformizing the legislation of his realm. It focuses on legislative issues, but also moral ones.

ordenamiento_de_alcala_policy.name: Ordenamiento de Alcalá
ordenamiento_de_alcala_policy.desc: The Ordenamiento de Alcalá is a legal code that unifies and centralizes our diverse laws, asserting central authority over local customs and privileges.

statutes_of_lithuania_policy.name: Statutes of
statutes_of_lithuania_policy.desc: A series of codified laws aimed at confirming the legal responsibilities and framework of the elites, as well as promoting a wave of centralization.

lit_casimir_code_policy.name: Sudebnik of Lithuania
lit_casimir_code_policy.desc: To combat the lack of a code within the nation, as well as the criminal activity conducted by those of the higher strata, the Sudebnik of Lithuania was writen in order to properly rein in the chaos, as well as give more power to the .

articles_of_agreement.name: Articles of Agreement
articles_of_agreement.desc: The Articles of Agreement are the cornerstone of the social order on board a pirate ship. They guarantee that every crewman has an equal vote in all matters and an equal share of all plunder. Articles such as these should be established for the republic itself, so that the liberty and equality of all pirates is secured.

tur_kanum_i_osmani.name: kanun‐i Osmani
tur_kanum_i_osmani.desc: A collection of legislations that together make up the laws of , focused on providing internal stability for the numerous ethnicities rather than on conquering new lands.

ara_royal_ordinances_policy.name: Royal Ordinances
ara_royal_ordinances_policy.desc: The Royal Ordinances are a set of statutes issued to regulate various aspects of the royal court and household. These rules outline the roles and responsibilities of court officials and include detailed provisions for the coronation ceremony of Aragonese kings.

mongol_law_policy.name: Mongol Law
mongol_law_policy.desc: Although secret from the public, the Mongol Law aimed for three things: obedience to the current ruler, binding together the people, and severely punishing any wrongdoing to the state. By keeping it secret from the public it can also be more easily changed to suit any other needs.

nueva_recopilacion_policy.name: Nueva Recopilación
nueva_recopilacion_policy.desc: A new compilation of the numerous laws within our realm, they will allow us to properly centralize and ensure control over our territories.

couteume_de_normaundie.name: Coutume de Normandie
couteume_de_normaundie.desc: The codified customs of the emphasize feudal land rights, noble privilege, and local autonomy. While favoring a decentralized and traditional society, these laws form a robust legal framework that ensures the power of the nobility and preserves the distinct identity of the .

new_corpus_juris_civilis.name: Corpus Juris Civilis
new_corpus_juris_civilis.desc: The great compilation of Roman law, ordered under Emperor Justinian, gathered centuries of rulings, edicts, and wisdom into a single body. The Codex, Digest, Institutes, and Novellae together have once again become the backbone of governance and justice, ensuring our authority, legal consistency, and the proper conduct of our government.

assizes_of_romania_policy.name: Assizes of Romania
assizes_of_romania_policy.desc: The Assizes of Romania codifies Francien feudal law within the Latin East, establishing a rigid hierarchy between the rulers and their vassal lords. It empoweres the High Court to mediate disputes over fiefs and military service while enforcing a dual social system that keeps the Greek peasantry in semi-servitude. This legal framework provides the structural continuity that allows the Frankokratia to endure as a Latin-governed society.

carta_de_logu_policy.name: Carta de Logu
carta_de_logu_policy.desc: Emerging from the Giudicato of Arborea, this is one of the first comprehensive legal codes in Europe written in a Romance vernacular (Sardinian). It establishes a culture of 'Rule of Law' that protects the rights of commoners and regulates pastoral land use. This legal sophistication allows the Sardinians to maintain a unified social fabric. It fosters a cultural identity defined by civic rights and a deep-seated respect for the collective ownership of the Logu.

anr_manual_digest_policy.name: Manual Digest
anr_manual_digest_policy.desc: A systematic manual compiled by the co-principality's jurists codifies Andorran customary law, providing clear precedent for the valleys' courts and reinforcing the realm's enduring legal traditions.

fuero_juzgo_policy.name: Fuero Juzgo
fuero_juzgo_policy.desc: The ancient Visigothic law code, preserved and adapted through centuries of Reconquista, remains the bedrock of justice in our realm — binding nobles to its precedents and legitimizing our rule in the eyes of the church and the people.

mll_dret_civil_policy.name: Dret Civil de Mallorca
mll_dret_civil_policy.desc: The Mallorcan civil law tradition, rooted in Roman practice and Catalan charter, governs property, contracts, and inheritance with a precision that fosters commerce and preserves the distinct identity of our subjects.

forestry_ordinance.name: Forestry Ordinance
forestry_ordinance.desc: Not every tree in the forest is suitable for shipbuilding. To ensure our ships are of the very best quality, we will by law require that any felled trees apt for building ships be immediately surrendered for that purpose.

mandatory_impressment.name: Mandatory Impressment
mandatory_impressment.desc: Every coastal settlement shall mandate naval service for their young men, who are to devote a minimum of one year to our fleets.

navy_audits.name: Navy Audits
navy_audits.desc: A fleet in disrepair can be a dangerous disadvantage in times of trouble. We will therefore carry out regular maintenance audits of our main shipyards and ports to ensure our fleet is in perfect shape at all times.

protect_trade_routes.name: Protect Trade Routes
protect_trade_routes.desc: The navy will guard our main trade routes in order to keep pirates and other undesirables away from our commercial fleets.

shipwright_standard_regulation.name: Shipwright Standard Regulation
shipwright_standard_regulation.desc: We will pass a law to create a standard for shipwrights in order to be more efficient when constructing ships.

ara_consulate_sea.name: Consulate of the Sea
ara_consulate_sea.desc: The Consulate of the Sea is a new quasi-judicial body that will administer maritime and commercial law.

nav_maritime_code.name: Navarrese Maritime Code
nav_maritime_code.desc: Based on the original Fuero of San Sebastián, the oldest maritime law in , this code applies to every port in our possession and details the rights and duties of their inhabitants.

kilwan_merchant_navy.name: Kilwan Merchant Navy
kilwan_merchant_navy.desc: Centuries of maritime wisdom and access to high quality cotton and lumber have given way to a most formidable merchant fleet. Equipped with cutting edge designs and new sail compositions, these vessels are the pride of our people.

smugglers_haven.name: Smugglers' Haven
smugglers_haven.desc: A pirate enterprise cannot function without a way to sell their stolen goods. We must ensure that conditions in the Republic are favorable for smuggling operations.

act_of_navigation.name: Act of Navigation
act_of_navigation.desc: The dominance of our foes must be contested across all our markets. Through strong central directives and preferential mercantilistic practices, we will attempt to give our merchants a clear edge over those of our enemies and rivals.

monogamous_marriage.name: Monogamous Marriage
monogamous_marriage.desc: Monogamous marriage refers to a cultural or societal practice of union between two individuals, based on established customs, values, and norms.

muslim_marriage.name: Nikāḥ
muslim_marriage.desc: Nikāḥ in Islamic culture is the solemn and legally binding marriage contract between a man and a woman.

adamite_marriage.name: Communal Living
adamite_marriage.desc: The Adamite sect rejects the concept of traditional marriage, preferring to live within communal structures without a clear hierarchy.

polygyny.name: Polygyny
polygyny.desc: Marriage between a man and multiple women is seen as a sign of wealth and power within many communities.

dishu_system.name: Díshù System
dishu_system.desc: The Díshù System allows the practice of entertaining concubines at court in order to secure heirs.

celibacy.name: Celibacy
celibacy.desc: Celibacy refers to the state of abstaining from marriage and sexual relations. It is a choice often tied to religious or personal beliefs, emphasizing a life without a romantic or sexual partner.

all_cultures.name: Inclusive Levies
all_cultures.desc: Our people will share the burden when there is a call to arms, regardless of their culture of origin.

noble_levies.name: Noble Levies
noble_levies.desc: The Nobility of our country will lead our calls to arms, since they are the most willing and prepared for war.

ton_ta_jon_ta_ni_woro.name: Ton-ta-jon-ta-ni-woro
ton_ta_jon_ta_ni_woro.desc: In the early days of our empire, our army was made up of sixteen clans whose leaders promised to protect the great rank_empire_mali_ruler_male and the State. Translated as 'the Sixteen Slaves that carry the Bow', the Ton-ta-jon-ta-ni-woro are the high Nobility of the country and serve as commanders of the cavalry.

peasant_levies.name: Peasant Levies
peasant_levies.desc: The Commoners make up the bulk of our levies, so we must take care to recruit as many as possible when the need arises.

longbow_competitions.name: Longbow Competitions
longbow_competitions.desc: On holidays, every man in the country will take up bows and arrows, and practice archery. This will win us high honor in battle, and ensure we profit from our warlike enterprises. With the common folk so trained, our levies can march to war as skilled longbowmen rather than as ordinary militia.

zamanitchka_voyska.name: Zamanička Vojska
zamanitchka_voyska.desc: Meaning 'All Together', this system of universal military obligation demands that all able-bodied citizens, regardless of age or gender, are expected to defend the homeland when threatened. Unlike professional armies or feudal levies, this mobilizes the entire population to protect their independence, reflecting a communal commitment to defending their nation.

paik_system.name: Paik System
paik_system.desc: The Paik System is a corvée labor system where capable adults, the so-called Paiks, are obligated to serve in the state militia in exchange for farmland.

alarde.name: Alarde
alarde.desc: Alarde is a system of levy recruitment that assigns cities of the realm the annual responsibility of organizing several alardes, a type of military parade used to train troops. This keeps them fit and ready for military campaigns when required.

german_mining_law.name: Bergordnung
german_mining_law.desc: Control over the mining privileges rests in the hand of the state, allowing for flexible and efficient mining operations.

zimbabwe_mining_law.name: Direct Control of the Ruler
zimbabwe_mining_law.desc: All rare minerals are directly owned by our ruler, giving them ultimate control over any extraction operations.

nobles_mining_law.name: Nobility-Controlled Mining Operations
nobles_mining_law.desc: The Nobility controls all mining operations.

burghers_mining_law.name: Burghers-Controlled Mining Operations
burghers_mining_law.desc: The Burghers control all mining operations.

peasants_mining_law.name: Commoner-Controlled Mining Operations
peasants_mining_law.desc: The Commoners controls all mining operations.

novo_brdo_mining_law.name: Novo Brdo Code
novo_brdo_mining_law.desc: The Novo Brdo Code provides detailed guidelines on property rights, safety measures, and economic practices, significantly influencing the development and prosperity of our mining communities.

royal_fifth_law.name: Royal Fifth
royal_fifth_law.desc: As per the monarch's ancient patrimonial rights, the Crown is entitled to the natural riches of the land. However, such an arrangement would be tyrannical, so this natural right has been reduced to a simple twenty percent tax on all precious metals produced in the country and its colonies.

state_piracy_policy.name: State Piracy
state_piracy_policy.desc: Our nation fully embraces acts of piracy against our enemies. Our reputation may suffer for using these tactics, but the economic benefits can be enormous.

modifiers.label: Can be Target of Casus Belli
modifiers.text: Can be Target of Casus Belli

issue_letter_of_marque_policy.name: Letters of Marque
issue_letter_of_marque_policy.desc: While piracy is not something we necessarily support, it does present a marvelous opportunity to pit career criminals against our enemies. We will issue Letters of Marque to privateer captains so they can freely attack our enemies' ships without fear of prosecution.

anti_piracy_policy.name: Anti-Piracy
anti_piracy_policy.desc: Our nation is devoted to eradicting any pirate threats that may arise. Any act of piracy will be punished and prosecuted, and ships conducting these illicit acts will be attacked without mercy.

sea_beggars_policy.name: Sea Beggars
sea_beggars_policy.desc: By granting several letters of marque to anyone wishing to serve us, we can expand our navy without needing to construct any new vessels.

aristocratic_court_policy.name: Aristocratic Court
aristocratic_court_policy.desc: The Nobility are an integral part of our government. In order to better control, reward, and gain support from these ancient aristocratic families, the Nobility are tied closely to the monarch and the royal court.

balanced_court_policy.name: Balanced Court
balanced_court_policy.desc: The royal court serves as the center of the state and culture. Administrative, diplomatic, and military actions are just as much of a focus of the court as the cultural and internal politics of the state are.

court_of_culture_policy.name: Court of Culture
court_of_culture_policy.desc: The court is first and foremost the household of the royal family, and serves as a center of culture and prestige. Governmental and administrative affairs are separated from court life.

itinerant_court_policy.name: Itinerant Court
itinerant_court_policy.desc: To better manage the sheer size of our nation, the royal court is not bound to a single location. Instead, it migrates throughout the land and manages local administration on site.

harem_policy.name: Royal Harem
harem_policy.desc: Much of our court life is secluded and gender-segregated, centered around a harem where enslaved servants and concubines vie for influence over the ruler.

military_court_policy.name: Military Court
military_court_policy.desc: Spending money on anything for the court beyond absolute necessities is a ridiculous notion that will only encourage complacency and laziness. The monarch will live a frugal live, and dedicate more of the budget towards the army.

humanist_court_policy.name: Humanist Court
humanist_court_policy.desc: Our court and our ruler must strive towards humanist ideals. We must become a prime destination for aspiring artists and philosophers.

timurid_court_policy.name: Timurid Court
timurid_court_policy.desc: While warfare is the lifeblood of the state, music, art, and poetry are equally essential to the greatness of our country. Cultural traditions from the lands we have subdued will no longer be considered alien, but be used to develop our cultural enlightenment.

valide_sultan_court_policy.name: Valide Sultan
valide_sultan_court_policy.desc: 'Paradise lies at the feet of your mother', and as such, the queen mother should hold the highest position at court, have the right to oversee council meetings, and through her wisdom and benevolence, play an important role in most affairs of the state.

foreign_court_customs_policy.name: Foreign Customs
foreign_court_customs_policy.desc: Instead of depending on our own culture, we can take inspiration from other courts in order to further strenghthen our owm.

byz_porphyrogennetos_court_policy.name: Porphyrogénitus Court
byz_porphyrogennetos_court_policy.desc: An emperor born in the sacred Purple Chamber of the Great Palace carries an aura of legitimacy unmatched by any rival. Our court ceremony, codified in the De Ceremoniis, projects the majesty of a living Roman Empire to every envoy who enters our capital. The elaborate protocol is costly, but the prestige it radiates solidifies the dynasty's claim before the world.

ara_italian_dual_court.name: Dual Court in Italy
ara_italian_dual_court.desc: By establishing two courts within our realm, we can manage both sides without needing to rely on the local nobility.

hanafi_policy.name: Ḥanafī Jurisprudence
hanafi_policy.desc: The Ḥanafī Madhhab is named after Abū Ḥanīfa Al-Nu'mān ibn Thābit. The school originated in Kufa and is prominent throughout the Farsi and world, including northern India. Though textual sources in the common_string_quran and Ḥadīth are given preference, Ḥanafī followers have an inclusive view of sources and also employ analogy (Qiyās), juristic discretion (Istiḥsan), and local customs ('Urf) in their jurisprudence. Some view it as the most flexible of the schools.

hanbali_policy.name: Ḥanbalī Jurisprudence
hanbali_policy.desc: The Ḥanbalī Madhhab is named after Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, and champions withholding from any speculative theology, Kalām. Ḥanbalī followers maintain that the common_string_quran and Sunnah are the only proper sources of jurisprudence and that they should be interpreted in a literal and traditionalist sense. Though it is accepted as a valid Madhhab, very few states actively promote the Ḥanbalī school, and it was banned by the Abbasid Caliphs.

maliki_policy.name: Mālikī Jurisprudence
maliki_policy.desc: The Mālikī Madhhab is named after Mālik ibn Anas and is prominent in particular throughout and Iberia. Jurisprudence is primarily based on the work and interpretations of ibn Anas and his student Saḥnūn as described in the al-Muwaṭṭa' and the Mudawwanah. One of the foremost centers of learning within the Mālikī School is the Great Mosque of Āl Qayrawān, near .

shafii_policy.name: Shāfi'ī Jurisprudence
shafii_policy.desc: The Shāfi'ī Madhhab is named after Imām Al-Shāfi'ī, and it is prominent in particular among believers in Arabia, , and East . Unlike other Madhhab, the Shāfi'ī reject Istiḥsan and Istislah as sources of sharia, instead only relying on what is textually in the common_string_quran or Ḥadīth.

zahiri_policy.name: Ẓāhirī Jurisprudence
zahiri_policy.desc: The Ẓāhirī advocates for a strict adherence to the text of the common_string_quran, and focus on its external or apparent meaning. According to them, there can not be any conclusion drawn from reading the texts that is not in the texts themselves, otherwise Allāh would have explicitly expressed those already.

ismaili_policy.name: Ismā'īlī Jurisprudence
ismaili_policy.desc: The Ismā'īlī Madhhab is named after Ismā'īl ibn Ja'far, the successor of Ja'far al-Ṣādiq, and was the dominant school of faith in the Fatimid Caliphate but has lost much ground since its fall. The Ismā'īlī school encompasses a number of increasingly divergent branches, and in many ways, they focus on the esoteric elements of faith more than the or .

jafari_policy.name: Ja'farī Jurisprudence
jafari_policy.desc: The Ja'farī Madhhab is named after Ja'far al-Ṣādiq, the sixth Imām, and it focuses on independent reasoning by experts of Islamic Law, prefering that over analogy when establishing the Law. It also allows for a temporary marriage lasting a predeterminate period of time.

zaidi_policy.name: Zaydī Jurisprudence
zaidi_policy.desc: Also called 'Fivers', the Zaydī current is named after Zayd ibn 'Alī, the grandson of Muḥammad's son 'Alī, and follows his teachings as described in the Majmu' al-Fiqh. Zaydī followers emphasize justice and human responsibility and descend from those who supported Zayd's original revolt against the Umayyad Caliph. Zaydī people entirely reject religious dissimulation as practiced by many followers, and it is the most similar to Sunnism.

ibadi_policy.name: Ibāḍī Jurisprudence
ibadi_policy.desc: Believed to be a descendant of the Al-Khawārij, who first were supporters of 'Alī ibn Abī Ṭālib but later rejected his arbitration. The Ibāḍī school distanced itself from the Al-Khawārij following 'Abd Allāh ibn Ibāḍ, taking a more moderate approach and a more positive view towards different Muslim branches, having similarities with many of the other schools.

allow_slave_religion.name: Allow Slave Religion
allow_slave_religion.desc: Slaves have been already forced to abandon their homes and live a life of servitude under foreign masters. Let them at least keep their beliefs and rituals; it does not matter what they believe on the inside as long as they obey.

force_slave_conversion.name: Force Slave Conversion
force_slave_conversion.desc: How can we expect slaves to obey and be loyal if they are not willing to embrace our own beliefs, and instead cling to their foolish superstitions? Only by forcing them to abandon their heathenry and accept the true faith wholeheartedly can we ensure their obedience.

pa_move_towards_aristocracy.name: Aristocratic Support
pa_move_towards_aristocracy.desc: Our society requires constant reminding what our ideals represent. We must reinforce our values and elevate the nobility as the highest societal strata.

pa_move_towards_communalism_clergy.name: Support of Communal Values
pa_move_towards_communalism_clergy.desc: Our society requires constant reminding what our ideals represent. We must reinforce our values and nurture our communal roots.
